OGL-UK v3.0 grants a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, non-exclusive licence to copy, publish, distribute, transmit, adapt and commercially exploit the information, with attribution and the same-licence condition for adapted versions of official material. Class A (explicit open licence permitting redistribution and derivatives with attribution), so the standing defaults apply: our code and documentation are MIT, our rights in the derived compilation are dedicated CC0-1.0, and the source's own terms are preserved, never relicensed.

compilation.scope: Our contribution - the eligibility frame (domestic applications with parseable filing dates in 2010-2016), the registered-by-snapshot label with per-cohort censoring, the right-anchored recovery of embedded-pipe rows and stripped-string-key deduplication, the derived feature columns, the filed-year cohort partition with boundary-straddling exclusions, and the packaging - is dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0. The dedication covers only our contribution: the underlying IPO trade mark data keeps its own designation and remains subject to the Open Government Licence v3.0, whose attribution condition carries through to every copy of the derived data. Nothing here relicenses the source or presents CC0 as the source's terms.

source.status: UK trade mark open data (Intellectual Property Office, opendatadomestic.zip snapshot of 2018-02-13) under the Open Government Licence v3.0: free to copy, publish, distribute, transmit, adapt and exploit commercially with the required attribution statement. OGL-UK exempts personal data, third-party rights and official symbols from its grant; the shipped columns were chosen with that in mind: the source's applicant-name and hyperlink columns are excluded by design (build.py EXCLUDED_BY_DESIGN), and the remaining owner fields (owner_country, owner_region, owner_postcode_area - the outward postcode area at its coarse granularity), the trade mark text and the register's own classification fields are redistributed exactly as the source publishes them, with nothing added beyond our derived binary label, the class-indicator and count derivations, the filing-date eligibility frame and the partition. The derived dataset is labelled as such throughout and is not the IPO's official product.
